title: Cushion the fall

predict.q: Private investment falls by **100**. Households spend 80% of any change in their **disposable income**. The net tax rate is the share of any change in income taken in tax or made up by benefits. It rises from 0 to 0.25. What happens to the total fall in national income?

options.s: It gets bigger, because higher taxes take more from households.
options.fb: Higher taxes take more in good times, but in a downturn tax paid falls with income, which cushions spending.

options.s: It stays at 500, because investment fell by the same 100.
options.fb: The first fall is the same 100, but each later round is smaller because disposable income falls by less.

options.s: It gets smaller, because disposable income falls by less in each round.
options.fb: The total fall shrinks from 500 to 250: the multiplier falls from 5 to 1 ÷ (1 − 0.8 × 0.75) = 2.5.

options.s: It disappears, because the government replaces all the lost income.
options.fb: Stabilisers cushion only part of the fall; national income still falls by 250.

task: Move the **net tax rate** slider from 0 to 0.4 and watch the rounds of lost spending shrink.

target.do: Move the net tax rate slider to 0.25, then press Check.

takeaway: The stronger the automatic stabilisers, the **smaller** the multiplier and the milder the downturn.
